[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Latency Troubleshooting and SLOWLOG Analysis in Redis"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Redis is an in-memory data store known for its exceptional speed and sub-millisecond response times. However, because Redis is single-threaded for command execution, any long-running command can block the event loop and cause latency spikes across the entire application. Identifying and resolving these bottlenecks is critical for maintaining high availability."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Redis SLOWLOG"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Redis SLOWLOG is a system designed to log queries that exceeded a specified execution time threshold. The execution time does not include I/O operations like talking to the client, but rather the actual time spent executing the command inside the single-threaded command processing loop."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Slowlog Parameters"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can configure the slowlog threshold and maximum length dynamically at runtime using the CONFIG SET command, or permanently in your redis.conf file. The threshold is measured in microseconds (1 second = 1,000,000 microseconds)."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"# Set slowlog threshold to 10 milliseconds (10000 microseconds)
CONFIG SET slowlog-log-slower-than 10000

# Set maximum number of entries retained in memory to 1000
CONFIG SET slowlog-max-len 1000"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Retrieving and Analyzing Slowlog Entries"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To inspect the recorded slow queries, use the SLOWLOG GET command followed by the number of entries you wish to retrieve. The output provides structured metadata including a unique ID, timestamp, execution duration, and the argument list."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"SLOWLOG GET 10"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"An example output structure reveals important details:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"1) (integer) 12
2) (integer) 1638312000
3) (integer) 15200
4) 1) "KEYS"
   2) "user:*""},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Field 1 (12): The unique sequential identifier for the slowlog entry."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Field 2 (1638312000): The Unix timestamp when the logged command was processed."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Field 3 (15200): The execution time in microseconds (15.2 milliseconds)."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Field 4 ([ "KEYS", "user:*" ]): The actual command array and its arguments."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Latency Anti-Patterns to Avoid"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid using the KEYS command in production. It performs an O(N) full-key-space scan, blocking the main thread. Use SCAN instead."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Be cautious with large hash, set, or sorted set operations. Commands like HGETALL or SMEMBERS on massive collections block Redis while serializing and returning payloads."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid heavy Lua scripts that perform intense computations or iterate over large datasets."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Advanced Latency Monitoring via LATENCY DOCTOR"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Beyond SLOWLOG, Redis features a built-in latency diagnostic tool that analyzes recent events and outputs human-readable diagnosis reports and recommendations."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"LATENCY DOCTOR"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"By routinely monitoring SLOWLOG entries and addressing O(N) complexity queries, you can ensure your Redis deployment remains responsive, scalable, and performant."}]
